transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm here because I just keep blowing up at people. Over nothing, really. Like... I yelled at one of my employees the other day just for putting stock on the wrong shelf. I was actually shaking afterward, because... well, that's just not how I usually treat people.
Have you been feeling more irritable or angry than usual, even outside of these outbursts at work?
Yeah. I mean... like I just said, I just keep blowing up at people over nothing. It wasn't just that one time with the employee. It's... everywhere, I guess. I just... I don't usually act like this.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when you're not angry?
Um... no, not really. I don't think so. I just... I go to work, I come home. I haven't really noticed feeling down, just... what I told you already.
Have you noticed that your moods shift very quickly, or do you feel like you're reacting very intensely to small changes in your environment or relationships?
I don't think so. I mean... I already told you I get mad over little things, like the shelves. But my moods aren't just... bouncing around, if that's what you mean. I just get angry.
Is this pattern of anger and irritability something that has been happening for a long time, even before these recent incidents at work?
No. Not a long time. It's... it's just been the last couple of weeks. Ever since the fire in the kitchen, when we were... our first weekend working on the house. That's when it started.
Have you felt physically restless or like you can't sit still lately, especially when you're feeling angry or irritated?
Um, no. I don't think so. I mean, I get tense, maybe, but I'm not... I don't feel like I can't sit still. I just get mad.
Have you been worried about people leaving you or abandoning you, or do you find yourself getting very upset in your close relationships?
No. Not really. I mean, my husband and I have been arguing more, like I said, but... I'm not worried about him leaving or anything. It's just the stress from the house.
Have you ever felt unsure about how you see yourself, like your goals or who you are might change depending on who you're with?
No. I know who I am. That hasn't changed.
Have you found yourself acting impulsively or taking risks recently, like spending a lot of money, driving recklessly, or doing something that could hurt you?
No. I haven't done anything like that. I don't really take risks.
Has this anger or irritability caused you problems in your job, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Yeah... I guess it has. I missed a vendor meeting at work. And I actually walked out before my shift ended the other day. I just... couldn't be there. And with the house... I can't face going back there to deal with the damage. So... everything is just piling up. Work, home stuff... it's just a lot right now.
Have you had any days where you felt down or hopeless, even before this recent anger started?
No... I don't think so. Everything was fine before all this.
Have you had any days where you felt down, sad, or hopeless, even when you weren't feeling angry or stressed about the house or work?
No... not really. I mean, it's mostly just... the stress of everything. I wouldn't say I feel sad.
Have you noticed any days where you felt little pleasure or interest in doing things, even when you weren't angry or stressed?
No. Not really. I just... I don't think so.
Have you had any days where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things, even when there wasn’t a stressful event like the fire or work problems happening?
I... no. Like I said... I don't get like that. It's really just everything going on right now. Before the fire, I was fine.
Have you had any periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing, even for a short time?
No... not at all. I definitely don't feel energetic. I'm just... tired.
Can you tell me more about what happened during the fire? Did you feel in danger or experience something particularly frightening during that event?
I... I don't really want to go into the details. It was just... a fire. It was bad. I'd really just rather not talk about it, if that's okay. I don't want to think about it right now.
Since the fire, have you had any upsetting memories, nightmares, or moments where you felt like you were reliving the event?

I mean... yeah. Sometimes. It just... it jumps into my head out of nowhere. Like, I'll just be picking up a pan to cook, or... or even just opening a spreadsheet for work, and... suddenly I'm just back there. I can smell the smoke, and I see the kitchen filling up with it. It just happens before I can stop it.
Since the fire, have you been avoiding places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah... I guess I have. I haven't been back to the house. I just... I can't. Even little things, like the mortgage folder, or... the herbs out on the patio. Anything connected to that day just... it makes my chest tight. I just can't make myself go near any of it.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of intrusive memories, avoidance of reminders, and emotional distress related to a traumatic event (the fire) strongly indicate Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1). Other disorders such as mood or personality disorders were ruled out due to absence of symptoms like depression, mood lability, identity disturbance, or impulsivity.

inference_history.note: The patient reports episodes of intense anger over seemingly minor incidents, followed by distress and awareness that this behavior is atypical. This could suggest emotional dysregulation, which is relevant to several diagnostic categories including personality disorders (e.g., borderline, intermittent explosive disorder), mood disorders (e.g., depression with irritability), or stress-related disorders. Further inquiry is needed to determine temporal pattern, duration, associated symptoms, and functional impact.
